cards.explanation: The answer is False. Moses sets these cities aside "…across the Jordan to the east" (Deuteronomy 4:41). They are not in the land Israel is about to cross into. I think that's worth a pause, friends, because Moses says he won't be crossing the Jordan himself (Deuteronomy 4:22), and here he is doing a job on the side he'll stay on.

The one who could flee to these cities is the man who killed his neighbor by accident, with no grudge. The text says a manslayer could flee there after killing his neighbor "…unintentionally without prior malice." (Deuteronomy 4:42). No grudge, no plan, no malice beforehand. I think this is a heavy one, friends, but the text is clear about who the cities were for.

The word is life. The text says "To save one’s own life, he could flee to one of these cities…" (Deuteronomy 4:42). It doesn't say why his life was in danger, so I won't guess, bakers. What it does say is plain: running to one of these cities was how he could save it.

Each of these three cities belongs to a tribe of Israel, and look at that lineup, friends. Bezer belongs to the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead to the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan to the Manassites (Deuteronomy 4:43). Three cities, three tribes, and nobody had to share a cookie box. Moses sets the cities aside, and the verse puts a tribe's name on each one.
